newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank temporarily closes small bank.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank temporarily closes small bank.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Wednesday it has agreed to the proposal of Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank to have a bank holiday effective today prior to the rehabilitation of the bank.
It said Monte de Piedad, a small thrift bank, had been experiencing heavy withdrawals of deposits the past two days.

"The management of Monte de Piedad requested for the declaration of bank holiday so as not to jeopardise ongoing rehabilitation talks with prospective local and foreign investors," the Central Bank statement said.
The Central Bank did not say how long the bank holiday would last.
The "rehabilitation" would involve the infusion of fresh capital amounting to 3.1 billion pesos, the Central Bank said.
The bank ran into financial difficulties after 1.8 billion pesos of loans to thousands of tricycle operators and drivers went uncollected over the years.

The loans had been part of the pro-poor thrust of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Manila, which held majority control of the thrift bank until until late 1995 when it sold its shares to the group of banker Vicente Tan, the Central Bank said.
